settings.name: landmarkdle
settings.description: A DLE game about famous landmarks and structures from around the world.
settings.author: kitsune

categories.name: year
categories.description: Year the landmark was completed or opened

categories.name: country
categories.description: Country where the landmark is located

items.name: Golden Gate Bridge
items.description: A suspension bridge spanning the Golden Gate strait between San Francisco and Marin County.

items.name: Eiffel Tower
items.description: A wrought-iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris, built for the 1889 World's Fair.

items.name: Statue of Liberty
items.description: A colossal copper statue on Liberty Island in New York Harbor, gifted by France to the United States.

items.name: Colosseum
items.description: An ancient Roman amphitheater in central Rome that hosted public spectacles and gladiatorial contests.

items.name: Elizabeth Tower
items.description: The clock tower at the north end of the Palace of Westminster in London, commonly associated with the name Big Ben.

items.name: Sydney Opera House
items.description: A performing arts center on Sydney Harbour famous for its shell-like roof forms.

items.name: Taj Mahal
items.description: A white marble mausoleum in Agra commissioned by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in memory of Mumtaz Mahal.

items.name: Christ the Redeemer
items.description: A monumental Art Deco statue of Jesus Christ overlooking Rio de Janeiro from Corcovado mountain.

items.name: Burj Khalifa
items.description: A supertall skyscraper in Dubai and the tallest building in the world.

items.name: Leaning Tower of Pisa
items.description: The freestanding bell tower of Pisa Cathedral, famous for its unintended tilt.

items.name: Tower Bridge
items.description: A combined bascule and suspension bridge crossing the River Thames in London.

items.name: Brandenburg Gate
items.description: An eighteenth-century neoclassical gate in Berlin that became a symbol of German unity.

items.name: Sagrada Familia
items.description: A monumental basilica in Barcelona designed principally by architect Antoni Gaudi; construction began in 1882.

items.name: Notre-Dame de Paris
items.description: A medieval Gothic cathedral on the Ile de la Cite in Paris.

items.name: Arc de Triomphe
items.description: A monumental triumphal arch standing at the western end of the Champs-Elysees in Paris.

items.name: Mount Rushmore
items.description: A monumental sculpture carved into Mount Rushmore in South Dakota depicting four U.S. presidents.

items.name: Empire State Building
items.description: An Art Deco skyscraper in Midtown Manhattan that was the world's tallest building for decades.

items.name: One World Trade Center
items.description: The main building of the rebuilt World Trade Center complex in Lower Manhattan.

items.name: Space Needle
items.description: An observation tower in Seattle built for the 1962 World's Fair.

items.name: CN Tower
items.description: A communications and observation tower dominating the skyline of Toronto.

items.name: Tokyo Tower
items.description: A communications and observation tower in Tokyo inspired by the Eiffel Tower.

items.name: Tokyo Skytree
items.description: A broadcasting and observation tower in Sumida, Tokyo.

items.name: Petronas Towers
items.description: Twin skyscrapers in Kuala Lumpur linked by a skybridge.

items.name: Taipei 101
items.description: A landmark skyscraper in Taipei known for its stacked pagoda-inspired design.

items.name: Marina Bay Sands
items.description: An integrated resort in Singapore formed by three towers topped by a large shared SkyPark.

items.name: Gateway Arch
items.description: A stainless-steel arch in St. Louis commemorating the westward expansion of the United States.

items.name: Atomium
items.description: A landmark building in Brussels created for Expo 58 and shaped like an enlarged iron crystal cell.

items.name: Palace of Westminster
items.description: The Gothic Revival meeting place of the Parliament of the United Kingdom on the River Thames.

items.name: Buckingham Palace
items.description: The London royal residence and administrative headquarters of the British monarch.

items.name: Neuschwanstein Castle
items.description: A nineteenth-century historicist castle in Bavaria commissioned by King Ludwig II.

items.name: Himeji Castle
items.description: A large Japanese hilltop castle complex famous for its white exterior and surviving feudal architecture.

items.name: Edinburgh Castle
items.description: A historic fortress dominating the skyline of Edinburgh from Castle Rock.

items.name: Parthenon
items.description: An ancient Greek temple on the Athenian Acropolis dedicated to the goddess Athena.

items.name: Pantheon
items.description: An ancient Roman building in Rome famous for its vast concrete dome and central oculus.

items.name: Angkor Wat
items.description: A vast twelfth-century temple complex in Cambodia and one of the world's largest religious monuments.

items.name: Borobudur
items.description: A massive ninth-century Buddhist temple in Central Java built as a stepped monument with hundreds of stupas.

items.name: Kinkaku-ji
items.description: A Zen Buddhist temple in Kyoto whose upper floors are covered in gold leaf.

items.name: Hagia Sophia
items.description: A monumental domed structure in Istanbul that has served as a church, mosque, and museum during its history.

items.name: Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque
items.description: A monumental white marble mosque in Abu Dhabi known for its domes, courtyards, and large prayer hall.

items.name: Saint Basil's Cathedral
items.description: A colorful Orthodox church on Red Square in Moscow known for its distinctive onion domes.

items.name: Florence Cathedral
items.description: The cathedral of Florence, renowned for Filippo Brunelleschi's enormous masonry dome.

items.name: St. Peter's Basilica
items.description: A major Renaissance church in Vatican City built over the traditional burial site of Saint Peter.

items.name: Great Wall of China
items.description: A vast network of fortifications built and rebuilt across northern China over many centuries; this date represents the start of major Ming construction.

items.name: Machu Picchu
items.description: A fifteenth-century Inca citadel set high in the Andes above the Sacred Valley.

items.name: Petra
items.description: An ancient Nabataean city in southern Jordan famous for monumental architecture carved directly into sandstone cliffs.

items.name: Chichen Itza
items.description: A major Maya city on the Yucatan Peninsula containing the famous stepped pyramid El Castillo.

items.name: Great Pyramid of Giza
items.description: The largest of the Giza pyramids, built as the tomb of the pharaoh Khufu and the oldest surviving Ancient Wonder.

items.name: Stonehenge
items.description: A prehistoric stone circle on Salisbury Plain in southern England.

items.name: Moai of Easter Island
items.description: Monumental human figures carved by the Rapa Nui people on Easter Island, with production beginning around the thirteenth century.

items.name: Louvre Pyramid
items.description: The glass-and-metal pyramid in the Cour Napoleon that serves as the main entrance to the Louvre Museum.

items.name: Guggenheim Museum Bilbao
items.description: A titanium-clad contemporary art museum in Bilbao designed by architect Frank Gehry.

items.name: Burj Al Arab
items.description: A sail-shaped luxury hotel built on an artificial island off the coast of Dubai.

items.name: The Gherkin
items.description: A distinctive rounded skyscraper at 30 St Mary Axe in the City of London.

items.name: The Shard
items.description: A glass-clad pyramidal skyscraper in London designed by Renzo Piano.

items.name: Millau Viaduct
items.description: A cable-stayed motorway bridge crossing the Tarn valley near Millau in southern France.

items.name: Akashi Kaikyo Bridge
items.description: A major suspension bridge linking Kobe with Awaji Island across the Akashi Strait.

items.name: Szechenyi Chain Bridge
items.description: A historic suspension bridge across the Danube connecting Buda and Pest.

items.name: Channel Tunnel
items.description: A rail tunnel beneath the English Channel linking the United Kingdom and France.

items.name: Hoover Dam
items.description: A massive concrete arch-gravity dam on the Colorado River between Nevada and Arizona.

items.name: Panama Canal
items.description: An artificial waterway across Panama connecting the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.

items.name: Beijing National Stadium
items.description: The Bird's Nest stadium built for the 2008 Summer Olympics in Beijing.

items.name: Wembley Stadium
items.description: A major football stadium in London recognizable by its large arch.

items.name: Maracana Stadium
items.description: A famous football stadium in Rio de Janeiro opened for the 1950 FIFA World Cup.

items.name: Olympiastadion Munich
items.description: The main stadium of Munich's 1972 Olympic Park, known for its sweeping tensile roof.
